title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows, bump GH Actions and Node deps
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Consolidates CI workflows (lint, test, release) into fewer jobs, upgrades GH Actions and Node versions across workspace, adds caching + parallelism improvements, and removes legacy task runners. No behavior changes to runtime code. Expect faster CI and fewer flakes.
body:
Context and motivation: Over the last 18 months we accumulated many duplicated GH Actions workflows across packages (lint/test/release), causing long maintenance cycles and subtle inconsistencies in envs (Node versions, action versions, cache keys). This PR unifies the lint/test/release pipelines into a small set of well-documented workflows, upgrades GH Actions (actions/checkout, setup-node, cache) to the latest pinned versions, standardizes Node to 20.x in all build matrices, simplifies matrix combinations to reduce queue pressure, and improves caching/parallelism to reduce run time and flakiness.

What changed (high-level):
- Consolidated .github/workflows/* into ci-lint.yml, ci-test.yml, and ci-release.yml with shared composite actions for common steps.
- Upgraded setup-node to v4, actions/cache to v4, actions/checkout to v4 and added explicit cache keys with OS+node+lockfile fingerprints.
- Standardized Node 20 in top-level package.json scripts and updated workspace package.json files to accept NODE_MAJOR=20.
- Reworked test job matrix: split by package groups instead of every package, enabling parallel job groups and dynamic batching for large packages.
- Added a small composite action under .github/actions/common-build for installing deps, applying workspace-level cache, and running audit/lint prechecks.
- Removed legacy circleci/jenkins bridge scripts and unused scripts in scripts/ci-helpers/* (deprecated in favor of GH Actions).
- Small hygiene: removed old lockfiles from archived directories, updated CONTRIBUTING.md to reference new CI flows.

Checklist: 
- [x] Consolidate workflows 
- [x] Upgrade actions and Node 
- [x] Add deterministic cache keys 
- [x] Update docs and contribution guides 
- [x] Verify flaky tests and tune parallelism 

Testing and verification: 
- Local smoke: ran example packages (redwood-sdk-python, redwood, redwood-docs) through new workflows using act and in a forked pipeline.
- CI: multiple reruns on staging pipeline to validate cache hits and matrix splitting.
- Post-merge: monitored first 48h of main CI runs for increased cache hit rate and reduced median runtime.

Rollout plan: 
- Gate merged to main, keep branch-protection so workflows are updated atomically.
- If a package requires a legacy Node version, we will pin an override via a package-local workflow (follow-up PR).

Related: ENG-2345 (consolidate CI), PM-678 (reduce release friction).

review_comments: Alex Chen: Left a few notes about cache key determinism and potential race conditions when multiple setup-node versions are used. Asked to add node-major in keys.
Priya Kapoor (author): Responded - updated cache keys to include NODE_MAJOR env and fingerprint of package-lock.json / yarn.lock. Added comment explaining rationale.
Michael Thompson: Noted that the matrix grouping needs a fallback for very large packages to avoid OOMs on small runners. Suggested adding group size threshold.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added parallel-batcher.js and adjustable GROUP_MAX env (default 6) to limit parallel jobs per group.
merge_summary: Merged to main via squash. Commit message normalized to: refactor(ci): unify workflows and bump GH Actions/Node deps. Monitor main CI for first 48h for regressions.
post_merge_actions: Monitor main CI: watch for cache hit regressions and test flakiness for 48h
Open follow-up for package-level Node exceptions (if needed)
Announce workflow changes in #infra and update onboarding docs
notes_for_reviewers: Key items to verify: cache keys (OS+NODE_MAJOR+lockfile fingerprint), group size threshold tuning, and no implicit assumptions about older setup-node behavior. If you see regressions, revert to the previous workflow via the documented rollback steps in .github/ROLLBACK.md.
